_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the melting point of n-eicosane with the MACE-MPA-0 force field.

payload.task: Melting point of n-eicosane (C20H42) with MACE-MPA-0
payload.reason: Premise check fails: the property is well defined experimentally (310 +/- 1 K, NIST WebBook via tier1.json), but MACE-MPA-0 is not a credible model for it, and the run that would be needed is not affordable here. (1) Domain: MACE-MPA-0 is trained on MPtrj+sAlex inorganic PBE/PBE+U data, which has no dispersion correction and almost no molecular organic crystals. The melting of n-alkanes is controlled by van der Waals packing between chains. (2) Validation test (same model; scripts/crystal_check.py, 124-atom idealized orthorhombic herringbone C20H42 crystal, 2 molecules, ASE FIRE + FrechetCellFilter, float64, CUDA): starting from the PE-like subcell a=7.42, b=4.95 A (density 0.922 g/cm3), the fixed-cell stress was -2.3/-2.7/-4.4 GPa (ASE sign convention), meaning the cell wanted to expand strongly. The variable-cell relaxation had not converged (fmax 0.02 eV/A) after 1500 steps, and had already expanded to a=8.09, b=5.30 A, c=28.65 A, density 0.764 g/cm3. A 0 K density of 0.764 g/cm3 is at least 11% below the measured solid density of 0.856 g/cm3 (tier1, Shlosinger & Bentilla 1965), and a 0 K value should lie above a room-temperature one, so the model fails to recover an independent known result for this very material. The cohesive energy came out at -103 kJ/mol (fixed cell) and -206 kJ/mol (relaxed cell) per molecule, but I do not trust these: the isolated-molecule reference was only loosely relaxed. A lateral scan was also run, but it scaled atoms within each molecule, so it is not meaningful and I have discarded it. (3) Method: a credible Tm needs solid-liquid coexistence (direct heating of chain crystals superheats by tens of K). The interface would have to be perpendicular to ~2.7 nm lamellae, which means about 10^4 atoms and several ns per temperature with a 0.5 fs timestep (C-H). n-Eicosane also has a solid-solid transition around 305 K, about 4 K below melting. A number from an under-bound model would carry a systematic error of unknown size, so it would not be a usable result. Proposed well-posed alternative: use a dispersion-inclusive organic model (MACE-OFF24, or MACE-MPA-0 + D3(BJ)). First check it against the 0.856 g/cm3 density and against Tm of n-hexadecane (291 K) and n-octadecane (301 K) from tier1, then run interface-pinning or coexistence NPT runs at 290-330 K. Report the bracketing interval plus the error on the calibration alkanes as the uncertainty.

summary: refused: Melting point of n-eicosane (C20H42) with MACE-MPA-0 (Premise check fails: the property is well defined experimentally (310 +/- 1 K, NIST WebBook via tier)
